seoTitle: How to Withdraw Money From Stripe to Your Bank
metaDescription: Transfer your Stripe balance to your bank account by verifying your bank details and setting up automatic or manual payouts.
intro: Collecting payments through Stripe is only half the job — at some point that balance needs to land in your actual bank account. Stripe doesn't push money out automatically the moment it's charged; it holds it in your balance until a payout is triggered, either on a schedule you set or by hand. This guide walks through the Balances page where that money lives, how to attach and confirm a bank account, and the difference between letting Stripe pay you out automatically versus doing it yourself whenever you want.

steps.heading: Check your available balance
steps.body: Every Stripe account has a Balances page reachable from the left-hand menu, and it's the control center for anything payout-related. It splits your money into Incoming (payments still clearing) and Available (funds Stripe will actually let you move out), both shown as running totals. Before you try to withdraw anything, glance at Available — if it reads $0.00, there's simply nothing to pay out yet, no matter how the payout settings are configured. Stripe also surfaces account-level notices here, like a requirement to submit more verification information or a bank holiday that will push a payout back a day, both worth reading before you assume something is broken.

image.caption: The Balances page, with Incoming and Available totals and buttons for Top up and Manage payouts. Account notices about paused payouts or holiday delays show up right above it.

steps.heading: Add and confirm your bank account
steps.body: Stripe can't send money anywhere until it knows where to send it. From the payouts menu, open Bank accounts, and you'll see any account already on file listed with its bank name, currency, and the last few digits of the account number. Use Add bank account to connect a new one, or Edit account if details need updating. Depending on your country, Stripe may run a small verification step — like confirming micro-deposits — before the account is fully trusted to receive payouts, so don't expect a brand-new account to be payout-ready within seconds of adding it.

image.caption: The Bank accounts panel, listing a connected account with options to edit it or add another.

steps.heading: Set your payout schedule
steps.body: This is where automatic and manual payouts actually get decided. Opening Payout schedule presents two radio options: Manual payouts, where nothing leaves your balance until you personally initiate it, and Automatic payouts, where you pick a cadence — the dropdown defaults to Daily but can be set to weekly or monthly with specific payout days. Automatic is the better default for most ongoing businesses, since it keeps cash moving to your bank without you having to remember to log in. Manual makes more sense if you want to control exactly when transfers happen, for example to match them to your own accounting periods.

image.caption: The Payout schedule dialog, choosing between manual payouts and an automatic schedule with a configurable frequency.

steps.heading: Trigger a manual payout when you need one
steps.body: If you've set your schedule to manual, or just want money out sooner than the next automatic date, use the Manage payouts button on the Balances page and choose to pay out now. Stripe will offer to send whatever is currently in your Available balance, subject to your account's payout minimums and any country-specific restrictions. This is also the option to reach for if you've built up a balance and want to sweep it all out before a reporting deadline rather than waiting on the schedule.

steps.heading: Understand what affects payout timing
steps.body: Newly charged payments don't move straight from Incoming to Available — Stripe holds funds for a rolling period (commonly a few business days, longer for new accounts or higher-risk industries) before they're payout-eligible. Once a payout is sent, it still has to clear through the banking network, and that leg is affected by ordinary banking realities: weekends, and holidays like the Labor Day notice Stripe displays right on the Balances page when it applies. If a payout looks delayed, check those two things first — whether the funds were actually Available yet, and whether a bank holiday pushed the transfer to the next business day — before assuming there's an account problem.

faq.question: How long does a Stripe payout take to arrive?
faq.answer: Payout timing varies by country and account history, but it typically takes a few business days for funds to reach your bank, and bank holidays can add an extra day on top of that.

faq.question: Can I withdraw money before verifying my bank account?
faq.answer: No, Stripe requires a verified bank account under Bank accounts before it will send any payouts to you.

faq.question: Is there a fee for withdrawing from Stripe?
faq.answer: Standard payouts are generally free, though Stripe may charge for instant or expedited payout options depending on your account and country.

faq.question: Can I change from automatic to manual payouts?
faq.answer: Yes, open Payout schedule from the Balances page and switch between Manual payouts and Automatic payouts at any time.

faq.question: Why does my balance show $0.00 even though I've had sales?
faq.answer: New payments usually sit in Incoming for a rolling holding period before moving to Available, so a fresh sale won't be payout-eligible immediately.
